📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

David Storch had to make a major decision at Sheffield Wednesday recently by replacing Henrik Pedersen with Dave Challinor, which is paying off as he has sent an upgrade to the "unreal" Owls fans.

The goodwill towards David Storch and Arise Capital remains in place but they had to make the brave choice to sack Henrik Pedersen, with Dave Challinor coming in and winning his first two league games in charge.

Sheffield Wednesday are firmly in the automatic promotion hunt, let alone the play-off picture, following a 2-1 win away to South Yorkshire rivals Barnsley at Oakwell on Friday night. With other teams in the top half dropping points, they are well-placed to kick on.

It has been revealed that speaking after the Barnsley game on Saturday, Storch took to X (formerly Twitter) to outline his thoughts. He stated: "love all things Wednesday! @swfc Fans last night were unreal… we have the best supporters anywhere.

It has been revealed that "3 points away away away!! The energy, passion, devotion… You could feel it all the way to Chicago. Love you guys! Missing the live action so much. Hope to see you guys soon!

According to recent reports, "And thanks so much for all the well wishes. Getting a little stronger everyday! #WAWAW".

Storch is currently recovering from back surgery, but he will be delighted that his first huge footballing decision has paid off already, with Storch reuniting Simon Wilson with Challinor in the process.

It could prove to be a masterstroke for Sheffield Wednesday, given the pair's previous working relationship and the manager's exceptional record in the EFL. Challinor has repeatedly demonstrated an ability to build winning teams, secure promotions, and get the best out of his players, making him an outstanding appointment for a club with Wednesday's stature and resources.

According to recent reports, the pair enjoyed considerable success at Stockport County, taking them from the National League to League One, winning the National League title in 2021/22 and the League Two title in 2023/24. Challinor also boasts seven promotions across his managerial career, having previously enjoyed success with AFC Fylde and Hartlepool United.

Recent findings suggest that his Stockport side narrowly missed out on the Championship in consecutive League One play-off campaigns, losing to Bolton at Wembley in 2025/26 after finishing third. Wednesday should now have the ingredients to challenge for automatic promotion — and anything less than a serious push would be disappointing.

Many of the Sheffield Wednesday fans responded on social media to his update, with one replying: "Delighted to hear you're recovering well after your surgery. You made a great decision bringing in Challinor. A proper football man that'll help build us a club with identity. Look after yourself ☺️".

Another Sheffield Wednesday supporter added: "I have no nails left watching that last night! 😂 Fans were amazing could hear them so much on the TV. Can't wait to see them play at Hillsborough on Saturday! Get well soon Mr Storch. Positive vibes for you and the owls 🦉 💙 🤍".

Industry observers note that A further reply from a Sheffield Wednesday fan praised another aspect which has improved at Hillsborough, with one Owl stating: "Fab night at Hirsty’s social last night at the watchalong . Brilliant idea from the club".

Exclusive: Swansea City & Burnley in race to sign Huddersfield Town star Joe Taylor

💡 Key Takeaways

  • For clubs that have players that are starring in their leagues, they're going to face a fight to keep hold of them when it's all mentioned and done, and then there are clubs at various points in the standings of any division that are going to look to strengthen their options.
  • And for high-flying Huddersfield Town in League One, they have a number of players who may be of interest to teams higher up in the footballing pyramid than they currently are - one player is certainly being looked at by Championship clubs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The January transfer window is just over a month away from opening, with EFL clubs already scouting new potential players ahead of the month-long chance to bolster their squads.

For clubs that have players that are starring in their leagues, they're going to face a fight to keep hold of them when it's all mentioned and done, and then there are clubs at various points in the standings of any division that are going to look to strengthen their options.

And for high-flying Huddersfield Town in League One, they have a number of players who may be of interest to teams higher up in the footballing pyramid than they currently are - one player is certainly being looked at by Championship clubs.

Football League World has been exclusively informed that Terriers hot-shot Joe Taylor is a wanted man in the second tier ahead of the mid-season window.

Despite Dutch winger Derensili Sanches Fernandes taking most of the praise and plaudits for the West Yorkshire outfit since his summer arrival from Excelsior, Taylor has been quietly going about his business as part of their dangerous attacking unit, having forced his way back into contention at the Accu Stadium following his loan out to Wigan Athletic in 2025-26.

The 24-year-old was shipped out temporarily by previous manager Lee Grant to the Latics, where he found his spark again, scoring 11 goals in half a season for them before returning to Town in the summer under newly introduced head coach Martin Drury.

Alongside the aforementioned Sanches Fernandes in a supporting attacking role, where the pair play behind more of a focal point such as Ashley Fletcher or Bojan Radulovic more often than not, Taylor has found the back of the net 10 times in League One already in just 14 outings, proving to be one of League One's best once again.

And that goalscoring performance is not going unnoticed, with FLW exclusively being able to reveal that managerless Swansea City, as well as struggling Burnley are both weighing up a move for the Welsh centre-forward in January.

Taylor has only sparringly played at Championship level before for Luton Town before getting his move to Huddersfield, but there are clubs looking at trying to get the attacker a move up the pyramid.

Swansea of course lost head coach Vitor Matos to Strasbourg last week, but it will not stop them eyeing up targets ahead of January, and Taylor is on their radar, even with a strike-force of Adam Idah, Ross Stewart and Zan Vipotnik to choose from - the latter was the Championship's top scorer last season but has failed to fire in 2026-27, and theoretically could be cashed in on to open up the space for another new forward.

Burnley meanwhile are in the Championship relegation zone and haven't won in Fabio Celestini's four matches in charge - they have centre-forward options like Jamie Vardy, Zeki Amdouni and Andreas Hountondji, but with a lack of goals coming from that particular trio, Taylor is being considered as a January option.

Whether Huddersfield would cash in on Taylor mid-season with their promotion aspirations remains to be seen, but given he's under contract until 2029, it'll likely take a significant amount of cash to prise him away from Drury's squad.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A professional 1-0 victory at Lincoln City extended Wrexham’s unbeaten run to three games, having drawn with Wolves and secured a statement win over table-topping Middlesbrough.

According to recent reports, inconsistency has plagued the Red Dragons’ campaign so far though, struggling to rekindle the fine form which saw them go within touching distance of the Championship play-off places last season. But, Phil Parkinson’s side now appear to have found their feet.

After bringing an end to their five-game winless away run with a victory at Lincoln City, Wrexham are slowly but surely climbing the table and sit in 14th ahead of a trip to face a troubled Bristol City side.

The Robins have lost three on the bounce with pressure mounting on under-fire boss Michael Skubala after another underwhelming showing against Middlesbrough, although the Bristol City hierarchy have publicly backed him to turn them around.

Injuries have played a significant role in Wrexham’s slow start to the campaign, with influential forwards Josh Windass and Nathan Broadhead among those sidelined. Both are expected to return to action next month.

It has been revealed that question marks surround whether Oliver Rathbone will feature at Ashton Gate after being withdrawn on Saturday with a dead leg. Thankfully, Parkinson confirmed after the game that it isn’t a serious matter.

Callum O’Hare hasn’t featured since the defeat to Blackburn Rovers last month and remains a doubt with an ankle problem, while Sam Smith is a long-term absentee with an ACL injury.

In better news, New Zealand international Liberato Cacace, who is yet to make an appearance this term due to recurring calf injuries, is back in training.

Industry observers note that sebastian Revan is also nearing a return having been sidelined with a serious hamstring injury suffered on loan at Burton Albion in February. The 23-year-old is expected to be fit in the Upcoming Year.

Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Kabore, Whiteman, Dobson, Thomason; O’Brien, Rathbone; Moore.

The Wrexham side has remained largely unchanged since their much-needed victory over Middlesbrough, with Parkinson seemingly settled on his preferred starting team.

Anthony Patterson will be in goal after two clean sheets from his last three games. Max Cleworth has impressed recently with the experienced Joe Worrall alongside him and both will keep their places alongside standout performer Callum Doyle.

Recent findings suggest that the Red Dragons’ positive form has coincided with Issa Kabore finding his stride in a right-wing back position, which saw him register an assist against Wolves. George Thomason has been equally key on the opposite flank and netted the winner at Lincoln, so both start again.

Sources indicate that the midfield pivot of Ben Whiteman and George Dobson remains too, despite Ben Sheaf pushing for a place. Lewis O’Brien and Oliver Rathbone will be keen to impress once again in more advanced positions with Wrexham’s wealth of attacking talent waiting to return from injury.

They were sweating on the fitness of Kieffer Moore ahead of the trip to Sincil Bank, but he played the full 90 minutes at Sincil Bank and will likely lead the line.

Man United chief Omar Berrada distances himself from Man City's Premier League charges - as Enzo Maresca insists his stars are unaffected by guilty verdict

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (887 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER and JACK GAUGHAN.
  • Published: 12:41 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 12:46 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved in any wrongdoing at his former club Manchester City – but refused to rule out taking action against them if their appeal fails.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER and JACK GAUGHAN.

Published: 12:41 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 12:46 EST, 20 November 2026.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved in any wrongdoing at his former club Manchester City – but refused to rule out taking action against them if their appeal fails.

In his first sit-down interview in five months, broadcast on Friday, Berrada tackled a range of topics concerning United but his links to City, from whom he joined United in 2024, were also brought up. He worked at the club during some of the period that City were found to have broken Premier League rules.

Back in September, an independent regulatory commission found City guilty of a multitude of charges brought against them by the Premier League, with financial offences ranging between 2009 and 2018.

The scathing verdict determined that City had 'artificially inflated' their revenues and reduced costs through 'disguised funding' schemes such as 'sham' contracts.

Berrada joined City in 2011 before going on to become their chief operating officer in 2016, raising questions over whether he could end up implicated if City – who vehemently contest the charges – fail in their appeal.

It has been revealed that 'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted. 'I want to be very clear about this, right. I wasn't involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn't involved in the proceedings; there are no allegations against me, and in that sense there will be no surprises.'.

Asked if United would push for compensation should City's guilty verdict be upheld on appeal, Berrada remained tight-lipped.

Recent findings suggest that omar Berrada joined Manchester City in 2011... and moved across the city 13 years later.

Berrada has become one of the main sources of anger among United fans who have campaigned against the owners and the board.

In a recent development, 'I don't want to comment on that because right now it's an ongoing process,' he added. 'When it runs its course we'll take our view of where is our position as Manchester United.'.

Berrada was not used as a witness in the original investigation and there are no allegations directed specifically to the now-United CEO.

City boss Enzo Maresca, meanwhile, insisted that the guilty verdicts handed down to Manchester City for financial chicanery have not affected his players despite three consecutive Premier League defeats.

City fell six points behind defending champions Arsenal in the weeks before this month’s international break amid a slew of individual high-profile errors that led to claims of Maresca’s squad being preoccupied by the uncertainty surrounding the club.

The Premier League have a range of available sanctions to them were City to lose an appeal set for next month. Those would likely result in relegation to the Championship.

But Maresca does not equate that looming doomsday backdrop with a worrying run of form before they face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday lunchtime.

According to recent reports, ‘I don't think the players are thinking too much about that,’ Maresca mentioned. ‘If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, look at [Aston] Villa away. We had so many chances, for instance Iliman [Ndiaye] hit the post, or Brighton where the keeper was man of the match.

Enzo Maresca insists his stars are not thinking about the impact of the guilty verdict.

Erling Haaland states he is 'incredibly' happy to be a City player and tops the Premier League scoring charts with nine so far this campaign.

‘Then [Nottingham] Forest when Erling [Haaland] had the chance to score for 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise. I don't think they are worried about that.’.

Haaland claimed to be ‘incredibly happy’ about being a City player in a defiant interview with Norwegian television earlier in the week, although few others have addressed the problems publicly.

Marc Guehi has previously noted the players are ‘relaxed’, while Phil Foden refused to discuss it when asked.

Maresca has spent the past fortnight analysing City’s ten league matches and has admitted that the team requires more balance after conceding too many goals to turnovers or counter attacks.

‘I was not thinking that we were doing everything well when we were winning games and I'm not thinking that we did everything wrong when we lost games,’ the Italian added.

‘For me it is the beginning of something long. I think we are attacking well because we are creating chances and overall we are controlling games.

Sources indicate that ‘There are moments we are not controlling and we have to realise the reasons why and do better. We are conceding goals and most are avoidable from my point of view.’.

There have been occasions – like the first goal at Forest – when City’s building from the back has put them in serious trouble. Josko Gvardiol lost the ball at the City Ground after no midfielder had shown for possession.

Maresca mentioned: ‘We reviewed things during the break. The idea is to continue to attack in the same way and try to find the balance when we defend or when we are building like what happened for the first goal against Forest.

‘When you are building and you lose the ball in the build-up it's difficult to build with that.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Queens Park Rangers goalscoring icon, Charlie Austin, has hit out at Millwall boss, Alex Neil, following the Scot's criticism towards Hoops winger, Paul Smyth, following Saturday's heated all-London affair at The Den.

Rangers continued their recently impressive form with a third victory in five matches by defeating the Lions 1-0 in SE16, courtesy of Nicolas Madsen's strike in the first minute of first-half stoppage time.

However, it is fair to say that the remainder of the contest wasn't without controversy, as the hosts were reduced to 10 men just 15 minutes into the contest after Zak Sturge's late challenge on the Northern Ireland international winger.

Although the statistics certainly showcased that Julien Stephan's side could have won the game by more if they finished their 31 attempts at Lukas Jensen's goal, much of Neil's post-match press conference centered around Smyth's involvement throughout.

The Saturday lunchtime victory saw Rangers end the Championship's 16th matchweek in seventh on 27 points, whilst Millwall sit 16th with nine fewer points.

Smyth, 29, is capable of featuring on either flank, and certainly caused plenty of issues for the Lions defence on Saturday in his 74-minute cameo, although Neil certainly had differing opinions.

“I spoke to Smyth about diving on the pitch in general. We had five players booked, and most of them came from him falling over," he remarked.

“The sending off – if he’s not offside, he’s not offside. If it’s a sending off, it’s a sending off. I’ve always been really straightforward with that sort of stuff. If it’s found that he’s guilty and he deserves to be sent off, I’m not going to argue that.

Neil was also booked for a verbal altercation with the Rs man, adding: “I told him to stop diving.

“I think what it was, it’s an element of frustration, but I’ve watched Paul Smyth for years. He’ll probably come up here and tell you he never dives, but I’d beg to differ.”.

Austin is a former teammate of Smyth's at Loftus Road, having returned to W12 back in 2020, scoring 15 goals in 59 appearances during his second spell, which lasted for two seasons.

The 37-year-old now offers regular opinions on Championship developments, and he defended the 26-time international when asked on his YouTube channel to give a verdict on Sturge's dismissal.

Sources indicate that "I'm going to say yes," he noted. "Paul Smyth does well there. He gets his body in the way and knows what's coming.

"Alex Neil comes out and states he was diving all around the pitch. Shut up mate.

"You'd like to have Paul Smyth in your team," Austin stated.

"Seriously. The threat he gives when 'we' have the ball, but when 'we' haven't, he presses and uses his pace well. He entices defenders to get close to him, which brings a foul and he anticipates the touch is coming.

"He was great for QPR at the weekend.

"But, for Alex Neil to come out and say that, I thought it was a stupid and naive comment.".

Austin knows exactly what it takes to achieve promotion to the Premier League, having done exactly that with the Hoops and West Bromwich Albion.

The former striker was certainly encouraged by Rangers' performance against their London rivals this weekend, especially the way in which they continued to impose themselves on the contest despite the hosts' desire to remain defensively solid.

Rangers and Millwall fans, do you agree with Alex Neil or Charlie Austin? Comment below!

Neil's comments, unsurprisingly, split opinion depending on which side of the fence those who watched the 90 minutes sat on, but that doesn't take away from the threat Smyth can possess, with the attacker already scoring and assisting three goals this campaign.

Recent findings suggest that after a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With three wins in their last four matches, Sheffield United have found some form heading in to the busy December period.

And one of Chris Wilder's stars of the campaign has been Sydie Peck, who remained at Bramall Lane despite transfer attention from elsewhere, is operating on another level.

Peck went through the entire 2024-25 Championship season without scoring, but after notching five goals last season, he's already matched that tally from midfield in 16 outings in 2026-27 - adding three assists to that tally too.

Peck - who joined United from Arsenal's youth setup in 2021 - rarely plays together with fellow midfield youngster Oliver Arblaster, who came through the Blades academy, but they started alongside each other in the engine room in the 4-0 rout of Watford this past weekend.

That pairing has been a source of contention for many United supporters in recent times - Peck's run in the first-team on a regular basis only really began when Arblaster was sidelined with a knee injury two seasons ago, and the latter was left sidelined more often than not when he was fit and ready to return last year.

They worked pretty well together against an abject Hornets side, but Wilder seemed to object to a question posed to him about whether or not they can work as a good pairing on a regular basis.

Wilder seemed utterly bemused, noting they've only played together six times in midfield, winning three and losing two, and he believes that fans are waiting for Peck and Arblaster to 'fail' as a partnership for whatever reason - you can watch the full rant below.

Arblaster's emergence in Sheffield United's relegated Premier League team in 2024, following a stint on loan at Port Vale, was a genuinely exciting moment - despite the drop back to the Championship, United had a player that was ready to start week in, week out in the Championship.

Sadly, his knee injury set him back a year, but it allowed Peck to emerge from the shadows and become the player he has now developed into - whilst still a raw talent, there's a reason why Premier League clubs have been circling in recent times from the likes of Newcastle United and Sunderland.

If Peck continues to seriously impress, then Sheffield United will have a big decision to make in the January window should bids arrive at their door - selling Andre Brooks, Callum O'Hare and Gus Hamer for decent money in the summer though could mean the club are in a stronger financial position than many think.

Every player has a price though, and with January fast approaching, there's a chance that the Peck and Arblaster partnership may not have that much time to flourish.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan’s shirt sponsor Emirates are set to make a change ahead of the 2027-28 season, according to a report.

As per Footy Headlines, the ‘Fly Better’ text will be removed from the shirts of Arsenal, Real Madrid and Milan ahead of next season. Instead, the airline will simply display the word ‘Emirates’ across the middle of the clubs that they sponsor.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As mentioned, it will not take effect immediately and will be something that is adopted from next season. The ‘Fly Better’ tagline started being seen in 2020 as a new marketing slogan that replaced the iconic ‘Fly Emirates’.

The idea is to create a more ‘streamlined’ look on the kits, and that is also why we have been seeing leaked designs for next season that feature just the singular word.

Of course, this is not the only alteration from a kit perspective that Milan are gearing up for. In case you missed the substantial news of the past few weeks, Adidas are set to take over from PUMA ahead of 2028-29, for what will be a fourth stint as the manufacturer of the Rossoneri’s shirts.

It is believed to be a record-breaking deal at least in Serie A, one that will net the club around €500m over the duration of the agreement. For many, it is a welcome return to a brand that became synonymous with Milan given the length of their last stint as the kit maker.

5 players should follow Ernie Weaver out of Sheffield Wednesday in January

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1029 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways

  • That's the view of newly introduced Owls boss Dave Challinor, who has hinted that a few loan departures may be on the cards for some of the younger players in the squad who put themselves in the limelight during their difficult campaign last season under administration.
  • Wednesday's ability to build a squad over the past summer window has meant that, despite some fans looking forward to seeing these young players become the core of a latest-look side, they've fallen by the wayside.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield Wednesday find themselves in a peculiar position regarding their academy, as a lot of young homegrown talents introduced themselves to the fanbase at Championship level last season due to "circumstances," but now need to find regular game time elsewhere.

That's the view of newly introduced Owls boss Dave Challinor, who has hinted that a few loan departures may be on the cards for some of the younger players in the squad who put themselves in the limelight during their difficult campaign last season under administration.

Wednesday's ability to build a squad over the past summer window has meant that, despite some fans looking forward to seeing these young players become the core of a latest-look side, they've fallen by the wayside.

Challinor stated that Ernie Weaver, one of the early standouts from last season before being sidelined for the majority of the campaign with a foot injury, could be someone who leaves on a short-term deal in January, following the likes of Charlie McNeill, Cole McGhee and Reece Johnson, who all played some part in the Championship last season.

These five players should also be tipped for a loan move in the near future to get some valuable game time, too.

Dave Challinor namedropped a couple of other players who could leave the club on loan at some point in the near future. One of those was fellow centre-back Gabriel Otegbayo.

It has been revealed that the Irish Under-21 international epitomised the chances that young players got last season while the club was in administration. The former Burnley academy man made 35 Championship appearances last season, including a run of 23 starts in the final 25 games.

Otegbayo began this season as one of the first-choice defenders under Henrik Pedersen, too, starting four of the first five in league action and scoring in his one appearance off the bench against Bromley in that 7-2 demolition.

In a recent development, since that fifth game, though, the 21-year-old hasn't started in the league, and he's to feature in a matchday squad in League One under Challinor. Indeed, his only appearance under the new boss came in the 4-0 EFL Trophy defeat against Accrington Stanley.

Wednesday fans weren't too enamoured with his performances in the early stages of the season, and also feel that he could benefit from a spell elsewhere.

The other player mentioned by Challinor as a potential loan option was midfielder Jarvis Thornton, who signed a latest two-year deal with the Owls this past summer.

The 20-year-old has been at Wednesday since he was eight years old and was one of the many academy graduates who made their first-team debuts last season. He was one of the main features of their run to the EFL Cup third round, and he made 23 league appearances, too.

This season, though, Thornton has been one of the main victims of the midfield being strengthened at Hillsborough. The returns of Barry Bannan and Jaiden Heskey, plus the addition of Billy Mitchell, have made it difficult for him to get minutes.

His last league appearance came in that 7-2 win over Bromley nearly three months ago, and he's made a matchday squad just once since then.

The newly introduced contract ensures that the decision-makers at Wednesday think he has a bright future, but he may need to begin to realise that elsewhere.

Industry observers note that it was a proud moment for Sean Fusire against Accrington Stanley in the EFL Trophy, as he wore the captain's armband for the first time. Unfortunately, the Zimbabwe international hasn't been able to stake a claim for regular league minutes this season, though.

Industry observers note that the 21-year-old, unlike the others on this list so far, has actually spent time out on loan from Sheffield Wednesday. He spent the second half of the 2024/25 campaign at Carlisle United in League Two, but was then thrust into Championship action last year.

Only seven players played more league minutes than Fusire last season, but the full-back only has a couple in League One this year, coming on for the final stages of Henrik Pedersen's final game in charge at Doncaster Rovers.

Under Challinor, he has appearances in cup competitions, but hasn't made a league squad yet. You feel that, once the January window opens, he'll be one of the first out the door.

Industry observers note that it was a pleasant surprise for Wednesday fans to see George Brown starting against Accrington Stanley. It was the 20-year-old's first appearance in nearly 11 months after a season plagued by injury.

Like Weaver, it was a real frustration to see him sidelined during the campaign in which he'd have gotten exposure at Championship level. He scored twice in just seven second-tier games last year, including one of their two wins all year at Portsmouth, and looked very promising.

Industry observers note that he needs game time, but he won't get it at Hillsborough anytime soon. A good loan move away, perhaps at the top of the National League, could be massively beneficial to his chances of making it back in the senior fold in South Yorkshire.

There arguably isn't a more exciting talent on Sheffield Wednesday's books right now than Will Grainger. The Welsh Under-19 international only just turned 18 earlier this month, and broke through towards the end of last season, scoring in a 4-1 defeat against Oxford United.

He also extended his contract with the Owls over the summer, but he, too, has been a victim of the strengthening of the squad, especially across the frontline.

Sources indicate that do you think Will Grainger will be a major player in Sheffield Wednesday's bid to rise back up the EFL? Let us know in the comments.

Wednesday won't just be wanting to loan him out to any club for minutes; they'll be taking great care with this decision, as the 18-year-old could be a cornerstone of this upcoming era under the Arise ownership.

A good League Two move could work wonders for Grainger and put him in brilliant standing to properly break into the Owls' senior side next season, if they remain in League One.

Latest Update: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1690 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

It has been made no secret that Chris Davies' side are looking to reach the Premier League in the near future, with the 41-year-old receiving plenty of backing from Knighthead Capital Management during a near two-and-a-half-year tenure.

Birmingham's strong start to the Championship season followed an intriguing summer transfer window, but they were swiftly knocked off the division's summit last weekend after a lacklustre defeat to fellow promotion hopefuls, Stoke City, on Saturday.

It was an encounter in which plenty of issues which came to a head last season for Blues were evident, including a lack of urgency in attacking areas. As such, the debate has continued as to which areas need strengthening within Davies' squad with the January window looming large.

On top of such decisions, it feels inevitable that some of those within the Blues ranks may move on to new pastures, including rather luckless full-back, Lee Buchanan.

Buchanan's senior career began seven years ago, earning a first-team berth with Derby County under Phillip Cocu for the 2019/20 campaign.

It wasn't until the 2020/21 campaign, which saw the Rams narrowly escape relegation under the management of Wayne Rooney, where the full-back earned his major breakthrough with 37 appearances, being named the club's Young Player of the Season in the process.

During the early weeks of that particular season, Buchanan was called up to the England Under-20s squad, where he revealed that Rooney, who became his Birmingham boss just under three years later, predicted a bright future in the game for the defender.

“He’s England’s all-time top scorer so speaking to him obviously helps a lot," stated Buchanan.

“He told me to go out there and enjoy myself, to keep doing what I do for the club and that he’s sure I’d be fine.".

The 2021/22 season was a difficult campaign for Derby, although Buchanan was one of several academy graduates to emerge with credit for his performance levels at Pride Park which would have resulted in Championship survival, were it not for a 21-point deduction.

The defender was then the subject of a controversial departure to Bundesliga side, Werder Bremen, where he would link up with current Birmingham teammate, Marvin Ducksch, for the first time, making 21 appearances in the German top-flight before swiftly returning to the Midlands under current Rams head coach, John Eustace.

At 22 years of age, Blues certainly invested in Buchanan's potential in their first transfer window of the Knighthead era, with the left-back penning a five-year deal.

Three of those have now passed, and the defender's time in B9 has become one to forget, not least due to an unfortunate ACL injury which kept him sidelined between December 2024 and August 2026.

Buchanan has only played 40 times for Birmingham since his arrival in July 2023, with the bulk of said appearances coming during the club's relegation campaign of 2023/24, prior to Alex Cochrane's arrival.

Davies opted to select Buchanan during pre-season and in the 1-0 win over Swansea City in the EFL Cup first round following his recovery with the Blues boss saying: “I looked at him before the game and thought if he’s called upon he's ready to go now and it says a lot for the man, as well as the player.”.

In a recent development, whilst Buchanan's character has never been doubted, his long-term position at St. Andrew's is far from secure, and that was certainly the case in the summer window.

In January, Davies was in no rush to loan out the defender despite Kai Wagner arriving as back-up to Cochrane, and even though the German swiftly returned to Philadelphia Union, Buchanan also attracted transfer interest.

League One promotion hopefuls, Luton Town and Reading, were credited with interest, but, ultimately, a move failed to materialise.

At 25 years of age, Buchanan is set to be entering the prime of his career, and the chances of reigniting his career seem very little at Birmingham right now.

Cochrane has continued as Davies' mainstay following the exit of Wagner, and whilst Kristoffer Lund has also suffered injury misfortune this season, the seven-time USMNT international does appear to be ahead of Buchanan in the pecking order.

Blues fans, could Lee Buchanan have become a key figure at St. Andrew's without his injury woes? Comment below!

In January, there will be 18 months left on the full-back's contract, making it a prime opportunity for Blues to recoup some form of cash on his services, whilst allowing the player to rediscover form and match sharpness after just one competitive appearance 23 months.

Industry observers note that luka Modric may be 41 years of age, but he reveals no signs of slowing down. In fact, he remains crucial or both AC Milan and Croatia.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by pointing out that Sunday’s game will be a first for Modric, even given the hundreds of games he has played. The midfielder will face Frosinone for the first time, the 227th opponent of his long career (155 at club level and 72 for the national team).

In ten days, Modric will have gone from from London’s Wembley Stadium where he faced England, to the Opus Arena in Osijek, Croatia, where he beat the Czech Republic and played 90 minutes as captain, back to San Siro for the Frosinone game.

It has been revealed that yesterday, Luka returned to Milanello and trained with the Rossoneri, ready to take charge of the group again when the tournament resumes. He’s one of the eight players in the squad who have surpassed 800 minutes of total playing time across all competitions, including goalkeepers.

According to recent reports, the Ballon d’Or winner has featured 13 times this season, with 11 being in the league (eight starts), and twice as a substitute in the Europa League. For his national team, he’s appeared in six Nations League matches, four of them from the start.

It has been revealed that the match against Spain on October 6th was supposed to be his farewell to Croatia, but instead he was easily persuaded to stay and continue. He’s played 19 of the 21 matches since August, accumulating over a thousand minutes – 1,114 to be precise.

It has been revealed that modric scored for Milan at 40 years, five months and four days (the winner against Pisa) and is third in the ranking of the oldest goal scorers in the club’s history. Alessandro Costacurta is second (41 years, 25 days) and Zlatan Ibrahimovic is first (41 years, 5 months, and 15 days).

So, another record is in sight in the present, but what about the future? Modric is tied to Milan until the summer, with his contract expiring in June 2027. There are no further options for an extension but the relationship between player and club goes beyond written agreements.

Luka will decide his own future, as he did last summer, choosing to stay. He still wanted Milan despite being left behind without his family (who had since returned to Madrid) out of love for the Rossoneri. Next season, who knows?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 04:01 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:06 EST, 20 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino has warned that Manchester United cannot be stuck in the past as he begins the job of dragging the biggest club in English football out of the Premier League relegation zone.

Pochettino faces a huge first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, and he is determined to make a fresh start at United uninhibited by the history of the club.

It has been revealed that ‘We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy, in the way that we love to work. I think our job is to adapt and to go ahead a little bit,’ he said at Carrington.

It has been revealed that ‘The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear. It's an historic club with years being one of the best clubs in the world. It's difficult to find another club the size of Manchester United. It needs to be in a different place than we are now, no?

‘But I don't think too much in the past. If we want to create something different and positive, and the people feel proud about that, it's about building our own way here. Thinking on what happened yesterday is not going to help. You cannot be stuck in the past.’.

Pochettino’s appointment at United has been a whirlwind after the Argentine oversaw his final two games in charge of the US national team before flying through the night to start work on Wednesday.

Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time as Man United boss on Friday.

‘I think it's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool, and now our focus is 100 per cent on Liverpool,’ he added.

‘My first target is to sleep, but I cannot sleep – only three or four hours per day – but I think the target is to know the people, the staff, all the people here in the club, and of course the players and try from the beginning to have a positive impact.’.

Pochettino admits he has missed being involved in day-to-day coaching at club level, saying: ‘Of course, we missed it a lot. We are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass, we need to smell the grass and to help the players to improve every day.

‘It's true that it's a different job when you are in the national team, but I think we are much better coaches now.’.

The 54-year-old told United that he wants to be involved in the all the key decision-making and transfers despite only being named as the club’s head coach.

Pochettino demanded more control during his five years in charge of Tottenham, and the difference between manager and head coach has also been a bone of contention at United in recent years.

Manchester United travel to rivals Liverpool on Sunday searching for their first league win since August.

Ruben Amorim was sacked after taking on the United hierarchy over his job title, while Erik ten Hag refused to give up his power to veto transfers.

Pochettino said: ‘I know that being a head coach, I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday and I'm going to pick the starting 11.

‘I'm going to make the changes and of course that, in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen in the squad. That is (why) in the end, Manchester United is a football club, no?

‘During all my (career), when I started at Espanyol, head coach, coach, manager. In the end, it's not changing too much because I think the way that we work is indifferent to the title description.

According to recent reports, ‘If you are manager it’s not necessarily that you have all the decisions. Maybe you are a coach and have more power in the decision.’.

Pochettino revealed that he met most of the players individually at Carrington on Thursday, including captain Bruno Fernandes who cut a frustrated figure towards the end of Michael Carrick’s time in charge.

Pochettino confirmed that out-of-form Bruno Fernandes will remain as United captain.

‘Bruno is our captain and I think he's a very key player, but all the players need to feel that they are important from the top to the bottom,’ mentioned Pochettino.

‘Yesterday we spent three hours chatting in an individual way in my office with all the players.’.

Concerns have been raised over the players’ fitness and attitude under Carrick this season, with the statistics suggesting that United have not been running enough.

‘That's a good question, no?,’ said Pochettino. ‘It’s a debate that I don't like to go into because I think we cannot talk about things without context, and data is about context. I think it's very dangerous to talk. We are here not to denounce things, we are here to build something.’.

Pochettino later shared a message on Instagram thanking supporters for their 'warm welcome' and declared the Red Devils 'cannot afford to waste a moment'.

'An intense first few days. Thank you to everyone for a warm welcome,' the Argentine wrote.

'We cannot afford to waste a moment. All our energy and attention is focused on preparing for Sunday.

'We can say many things, but what matters is the work we do and what we show on the pitch.'.

Stoke City could have the chance to go to the top of the Championship on Wednesday night, depending on how results on Tuesday go, when they host Millwall and former boss Alex Neil at the bet365 Stadium.

Stoke have continued their scintillating run of form under Mark Robins with a 1-0 home victory over Birmingham City at the weekend, leapfrogging the Blues in the Championship table, and now sit only behind Middlesbrough on goal difference as things stand.

Depending on how Boro get on against Swansea City on Tuesday night, Stoke could go to the top of the league with another three points in this fixture, though returning boss Neil is bound to make it as difficult as possible for the Potters.

Millwall haven't been at their best as of late, with just one win in their last seven league games, but with just two defeats in their last 16 games against Stoke, they have more often than not had the upper hand in this encounter in recent memory.

For Stoke, Djibril Soumare and George Hirst picked up minor knocks against Birmingham and will need to be assessed; Ethan Galbraith could come back into the side after illness, whilst Millwall wait on decisions on Luke Cundle, Josh Coburn, and Romain Esse, as Football League World takes a look at each player set to miss Wednesday's clash in the Potteries.

French striker Lamine Cisse has shown sparks of his talent this campaign, particularly in the games against Bolton Wanderers and Watford, but has been out of action since being forced off in Stoke's goalless draw with Bristol City a month ago.

It has since been confirmed that the 23-year-old will likely be out of action until Christmas, providing George Hirst, Robert Bozenik, and Sam Gallagher with chances to impress Robins up top.

Veteran full-back Aaron Cresswell has yet to make an appearance this season after extending his stay in North Staffordshire for another year over the summer, having picked up an injury during pre-season.

Robins confirmed that the 36-year-old was back on the grass training last month, but he still remains some way short of fitness, and isn't expected to make a return to the pitch just yet.

Luca Bombino has found minutes at left wing-back recently following an injury to Eric Bocat and impressed, with the American looking to make his mark in the Championship following his potential $5 million (£3.7 million) move from MLS side San Diego late in the summer window.

After picking up a yellow card in the first half against Birmingham, Bombino mistimed his challenge around the hour mark on Patrick Roberts, receiving his marching orders, and as a result, will be suspended for this game, as Bocat or Justin Devenny will likely take his place on the left flank for the Potters against Millwall.

Ato Ampah has endured a torrid time with injuries ever since joining Stoke from Chelsea's academy for a potential £3 million in January 2026, with the young winger still yet to make a senior appearance for the Potters nearly a year later.

The England youth international was on the cusp of a first-team return in October before a further injury setback means he will have to wait even longer for his Potters debut, as the youngster will be praying 2027 is his year.

Onto Millwall now, as left-back Zak Sturge is set to miss the trip to North Staffordshire after receiving an early red card in his side's narrow 1-0 home defeat to Queens Park Rangers at the weekend.

This means Alfie Doughty could come back into the fold to face his former side on Wednesday, or Jordi Osei-Tutu could be preferred in that role.

Mathis Servais joined Millwall in the summer from Belgian outfit KV Mechelen to much excitement, but with just nine minutes of Championship football to shout about nearly six months later, it hasn't exactly been the dream start to life at The Den he would've hoped for.

A hamstring injury in pre-season forced him to wait to make his debut, and another injury sustained in the following international break has kept him out of action since, and it doesn't look like he will be ready for this one.

Arguably the biggest absence for Millwall is French defender Tristan Crama, who, after an incredible full debut year for the Lions, has struggled with injury woes this campaign.

The 25-year-old has been limited to just five appearances so far this season, injuring both of his ankles, and has been absent from the side since Halloween's 4-1 victory over Derby County, where he was forced to come off just after the hour mark.

Filip Marschall joined Millwall in the summer from League One Stevenage to provide an alternative option between the sticks to Lukas Jensen and Max Crocombe, but after four appearances, he suffered ankle ligament damage against Lincoln City.

Jensen has since returned to the side and is expected to start between the sticks as the former Aston Villa youth player recovers.

Ryan Leonard, like Crama, has been missing from Millwall's squad since the 4-1 home victory over Derby, and Neil issued an patch on the 34-year-old in early November.

Neil stated: "About eight days ago, Ryan Leonard contacted his knee on the left-hand side at our place. It’s been sore since, but it’s getting to the stage where the pain’s not dying down. We got it scanned, and unfortunately, Lenny’s got an glitch just above his knee. He won’t be back within the next month.".

Southampton are propelling themselves back up the Championship table and Tonda Eckert, who had doubts over his future for off-field reasons, is now set to stay for the long-term at St Mary’s – but that could affect three Saints players.

Having been kicked out of the Championship play-offs ahead of the final last season due to ‘spygate’, Saints began this season with a four-point deduction in the second-tier and the prospect of a big ban coming for manager Eckert.

However, Eckert managed to escape with just a suspended six-match ban and so the club have now been able to tie him down to a latest contract, too, ensuring the German is contracted to the south coast outfit until the summer of 2029.

Southampton eased past Derby County by two goals to nil at the weekend to leave them sixth in the table and just five points behind Middlesbrough, even with those four points taking off them at the start of the campaign.

Eckert is proving himself to be an excellent coach and having committed his future to the club, three players will now be looking for a permanent route out soon.

Having signed from Aston Villa in the summer of 2024 after previously impressing on loan at Preston North End and Middlesbrough in the Championship as well as an underwhelming stint in the Premier League with Sheffield United, Archer again struggled in the top-flight when with Southampton.

Having scored just two goals in 35 top-flight appearances for Saints as they succumbed to a humiliating relegation in which they collected just 12 points, Archer only notched four times in 30 Championship games last season – albeit with a slight improvement in his overall performance level before the end of the campaign before being an unused substitute in both legs of their play-off semi-final against ‘Boro.

Over the summer, he reunited with Will Still at Auxerre and has shone in Ligue 1 with six goals in nine appearances and, with no long-term future at Southampton, especially under Eckert, a permanent move in January or next summer feels inevitable.

Another loanee now destined to leave St Mary’s on a permanent basis is versatile Japan international full-back Yukinari Sugawara, who is currently out at Cagliari in Serie A.

Sugawara has been largely on the periphery of things in terms of the first-team picture in Sardinia, where he now a teammate of former Leicester City midfielder Harry Winks, and that is where he ended up at Southampton, too.

Having spent last season on loan at Werder Bremen in the Bundesliga, Sugawara’s permanent exit from Southampton has been expected for a while but, after a summer in which Eckert again sanctioned his departure, that is now inevitable. He is contracted to the club until the summer of 2028.

Upon their return to the Championship last summer, Southampton shelled out around £7 million on American forward Damion Downs but, from the off, he appeared to be surplus to requirements.

Injuries and generally average form eventually led to Downs being loaned out to Hamburg in the Bundesliga for the second half of last season, despite coming off the bench in Eckert’s first four matches in charge of Saints last November before his injury.

An indifferent time of it at the Volksparkstadion was then followed by the 22-year-old being shipped out to St Louis City on loan this summer, where he has failed to score in ten MLS appearances as the expansion franchise finished third in the Western Conference and now head into the play-offs.

Downs is contracted until the summer of 2029 but a permanent move away in the winter after the close of the 2026 MLS campaign feels inevitable, even if he hasn’t done enough for St Louis to take the plunge on him just yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield Wednesday boss Dave Challinor has revealed that he has made training more ‘competitive’ after his positive start to life in charge of the club.

The Owls made the decision to sack Henrik Pedersen last month, with Challinor named as his successor at Hillsborough.

Whilst it’s still early days, the ex-Stockport chief has enjoyed a fine start at Wednesday, having followed up a 3-0 win over Plymouth with a hard-fought 2-1 success at Barnsley on Friday night, which makes it consecutive league victories.

Even though there have been defeats in cup competitions, Challinor knows that he will be judged on whether the team can win promotion this season, so he will be pleased that the team have moved into the play-off places.

Of course, the challenge will be to maintain these levels over the course of the campaign, but fans are happy with how Challinor has made an instant impact.

And, speaking to the Sheffield Star, the latest boss has opened up on the tweaks he has made since his arrival, as he explained that he has called for an increase in intensity in training in a bid to improve ‘standards’.

“We've tried to make training a lot more competitive. Every game that we play, whether it's possession, whether it's a passing drill, whether it's a small-sided game, it's about winning. It's about being competitive. It's about driving standards. They've been great with that. I would hope that's played a part in what we've done tonight, and it will certainly help us moving forward.”.

Firstly, the Sheffield Wednesday fans will love to hear this from Challinor, as there was a feeling that Pedersen lacked authority at times.

Despite their struggles last season, the Owls managed to build a very talented squad by League One standards, and the aim for Wednesday must be to win promotion.

Challinor is aware that it’s a major ask to do that, and you win promotion by the work you do every day on the training ground. So, the quality is there, but the players must show that they have the mentality and drive to bring success to the Yorkshire outfit on a daily basis.

The manner of the win at Barnsley on Friday was impressive, as Wednesday were ruthless early on, and then they saw the game very well, as they limited the Tykes to few clear opportunities.

There were great scenes at the end of the game as the players celebrated with the away supporters, and it’s victories like that which help strengthen the bond at the club.

Now, the challenge for Wednesday is to keep building momentum, and they could be difficult to stop if they do get on a roll.

Will Sheffield Wednesday win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

But, after a difficult period, all connected to Sheffield Wednesday will be excited about what the future holds under Challinor, as they look to make it three wins on the bounce when they travel to take on Stevenage on Tuesday night.

Drone operator apologises for filming Mauricio Pochettino's first training session, while Man United must apply to close airspace if they want to avoid another embarrassing security breach

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026.

The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.

United suffered the embarrassing security breach on Pochettino’s first day as head coach after the 12-minute footage showing the Argentine and his staff working with the players at Carrington was posted online.

The owner of the account called CC Overview, who is known only as Colin, justified the intrusion by saying that the airspace over Carrington is unrestricted and the drone was operating legally within Civil Aviation Authority rules.

United will have to apply to the Department of Transport if they want to close off the airspace to avoid more unwanted drones.

CC Overview took the video down on Friday morning insisting that he was unaware of the significance of his actions.

He also clarified that neither Liverpool – who are United’s opponents in Pochettino’s first game at Anfield on Sunday – nor any other club were involved in the filming.

Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session was filmed by a drone and the operator has now apologised.

The drone user, who is known only as Colin, stated he had not broken laws but apologised.

United have declined to comment over the incident and it’s unclear if the club have made contact with him or involved Greater Manchester Police.

His statement read: ‘I would like to speak about yesterday’s incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.

‘My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time.

'I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

‘I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets.

'I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match. I would also like to state that Liverpool Football club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday.

‘The video has been removed from my channel. I have spent the past four years building up my YouTube channel and were well regarded in the fields I film and would now like to get back to building up my damaged reputation and making well received responsible videos. Thank you.’.

United say they will not pursue legal action this time but will not hesitate to do so if it happens in the future.

To stop drones legally flying over Carrington, it has emerged that the club would need to seek permission from the Government to restrict the airspace around the training ground.

Footage of the session was captured close to Carrington and uploaded online.

Sources indicate that there are tight controls issued by the CAA and National Air Traffic Services over flying drones of different sizes, and a code of conduct related to how they are operated. It includes sharing photos and videos that could be ‘unfair’ to anyone.

It states that drones over 250g should not be flown closer than 50 metres to people, and drones below that weight should not be flown over crowds.

Sources indicate that the drone and model aircraft code also states that you must ‘keep at least 150m away from residential, recreational, commercial and industrial areas’. It lists sports facilities as a recreational area.

There are also rules regarding privacy, which may well apply to United given that Pochettino and his players were preparing for a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday – arguably the biggest fixture in the English football calendar.

It states: ‘Drones users must always respect your privacy and not cause a nuisance. They must comply with the same privacy regulations as anyone who uses a camera or recording device.

Man United installed signs in 2018 warning that the use of drones over Carrington was 'strictly prohibited' and would be reported for prosecution.

It has been revealed that ‘If your drone or model aircraft is fitted with a camera or listening device, you must respect other people’s privacy whenever you use them. If you use these devices where people can expect privacy, such as inside their home or garden, you’re likely to be breaking data protection laws. Any photos or recordings you take may be covered by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

‘Let people know before you start recording or taking pictures. In some cases, this will be easy. For example, if you’re taking a photo of family and friends at a family barbecue. In other cases, this will be less practical, so you must be careful to respect everyone’s right to privacy.

It has been revealed that ‘Think before sharing photos and videos. Avoid sharing anything that could be unfair or harmful to anyone. Think carefully about who could see your photos and videos – especially before posting them on social media. Apply the same common-sense approach that you would with images or video recorded on a smartphone or digital camera.’.

According to recent reports, liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was asked about the drone on Friday, saying: 'It shouldn't be legal. There is a reason why we train behind closed doors. It's not nice for any club.'.

Latest Update: Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4076 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

Sources indicate that “I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a major career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Recent findings suggest that floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

Industry observers note that what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

It has been revealed that as impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

It has been revealed that allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has mentioned supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was crucial for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca remarked.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

According to recent reports, FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

Sources indicate that all told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Recent findings suggest that well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

It has been revealed that mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

It has been revealed that well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

According to recent reports, norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

It has been revealed that some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

Industry observers note that 17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.
